label: Security
title: Visible controls.
description: Opaque server-side sessions, Argon2 password hashing, secure production cookies, session rotation/revocation, exact Origin and CSRF checks protect API mutations. Workspace membership and role authorization precede protected object

sections.title: Implemented controls
sections.body: Opaque server-side sessions, Argon2 password hashing, secure production cookies, session rotation/revocation, exact Origin and CSRF checks protect API mutations. Workspace membership and role authorization precede protected object access. Private API responses use Cache-Control: no-store; public caches must never store account or workspace responses. Task revisions and artifact hashes bind approvals to exact content. Two distinct authorized accounts approve client and developer decisions. Repository execution requires an operator-created workspace/target/profile grant. Revoked members, sources, grants and stopped workspaces cannot authorize later publication. Agent instructions and retrieved documents never grant permissions. The web service has no code execution route. Workers use pinned local model digests, structured responses, bounded correction rounds and separate review contexts. Protected test answers remain outside the model and guest. Rootless gVisor uses a read-only minimal rootfs, no guest network, no host credentials, fresh case processes and CPU/memory/process/output/time limits. Candidate output is untrusted data.

sections.title: Main threats and responses
sections.body: This release requires explicit operator configuration, bounded permissions and verification against the intended operating environment.

sections.title: Operator requirements
sections.body: Use least-privilege service accounts and database roles, pinned SSH host keys, private database/inference listeners, maintained TLS, bounded logs, verified encrypted backups and tested restoration. Do not expose Ollama, PostgreSQL, Docker sockets or runner state to the Internet. Keep runtime secrets outside source, browser bundles, logs and command arguments. Restrict operator access using MFA at the access provider where available; application administrator MFA remains a roadmap item. Application-level authorization is implemented; PostgreSQL tenant RLS is a planned additional defense. Disk/volume encryption, independent penetration testing, supply-chain attestation, automated privacy erasure and continuous capacity testing require deployment-specific qualification. No scanner result establishes blanket security certification.

sections.title: Vulnerability handling
sections.body: Use the private reporting route in SECURITY.md. Do not post credentials, personal information or exploit details in public issues. Assess impact, contain/revoke affected access, preserve redacted evidence, patch, verify and publish an appropriate advisory. Keep incident chronology and corrective actions. References: OWASP session management, multi-tenant security, gVisor production guide.

label: Architecture
title: A system with clear owners.
description: This release requires explicit operator configuration, bounded permissions and verification against the intended operating environment.

sections.title: Trust boundaries
sections.body: This release requires explicit operator configuration, bounded permissions and verification against the intended operating environment.

sections.title: Durable work
sections.body: PostgreSQL owns run claims, leases, attempts, artifacts, approvals, audit events, delivery intents and receipts. Model calls occur outside database transactions. Fencing and revision checks prevent stale workers from publishing. Workspace stop, source/member revocation and repository grant changes serialize with publication. An acknowledged change prevents subsequent publication or waits for the bounded in-flight operation. Git preparation occurs in an isolated clone with installed hooks. Publication compares the expected reference atomically and uses the native index lock. An uncertain post-publication result stays reserved for read-only reconciliation. Dedicated operator-owned repositories must not be edited manually during installation.

sections.title: Operational boundaries
sections.body: Project-specific services, users, storage, private listeners, resource limits and versioned releases isolate the application on shared infrastructure. General shell execution, arbitrary languages, automatic deployment to customer infrastructure, remote providers and external publishing connectors require additional engineering and authorization. Tenant RLS, administrator MFA and multi-region failover remain roadmap gates; application authorization and restricted database roles are the present boundary.

label: API roadmap
title: A contract before a connection.
description: 1. GET /auth/session establishes an anonymous HttpOnly cookie and returns a CSRF token. 2. POST /auth/login accepts email/password with Origin and X-CSRF-Token headers; successful authentication rotates the session. 3. Preserve th

sections.title: Authentication
sections.body: The authenticated control plane uses /api/v1 for saved workspaces, tasks, scoped sources, runs, approvals and delivery receipts. Read the OpenAPI contract and establish a session/CSRF token before protected mutations. Enrollment is operator-managed.

sections.title: Resources
sections.body: Inspect OpenAPI for exact methods, schemas and paths. All writes require session/CSRF validation; object access additionally requires workspace membership and the appropriate role. Repository grants have no self-authorizing HTTP route.

sections.title: Limits, errors and compatibility
sections.body: The v1 wire contract limits names to 80 characters, titles to 100, ordinary text to 4,000, artifacts to 20,000 and criteria to 20. Passwords require 12–128 characters. Settings own body, list, task/source/run quotas and request budgets. Responses use stable error codes, including 401 authentication, 403 permission/CSRF, 404 inaccessible objects, 409 stale/conflicting work, 422 invalid input, 429 exhausted budget and 503 unavailable readiness. Lists are bounded, not an unbounded historical export API. Mutations use task revisions and action request keys where supported. Reusing keys cannot create duplicate consequential actions. Following a timeout, inspect the recorded run/delivery before retrying. Breaking wire-contract changes require a new API version and migration notes.

label: Scalability
title: A million connections needs a workload.
description: These are planning assumptions. Validate read/write mix, tenant skew, payload distribution, data size, cache hit ratio, event fan-out, geographic latency and burst duration before sizing. The current control UI polls every three s

sections.title: Workload assumptions
sections.body: The future envelope is 1M+ simultaneous users. Connected sessions, active users, API requests and running AI jobs have separate planning assumptions. Qualify traffic, storage, queues, inference capacity, failover and costs in stages before each expansion.

sections.title: Architecture stages
sections.body: A stage is entered only after its previous workload envelope meets latency, error, correctness and recovery criteria. Add partitioning or read replicas only when measured query and write patterns justify them. Avoid giving every browser a database connection. PostgreSQL pools need a host-wide connection budget across all replicas and workers.

sections.title: AI and execution capacity
sections.body: Use durable admission queues, per-tenant concurrency/token budgets, queue deadlines, cancellation and backpressure. Size local inference from measured tokens/second, prompt/context length, output length, model memory and review multiplier. Size sandbox workers from measured case runtime and resource envelopes. Approximate required busy inference slots as admitted jobs/second × measured service seconds/job, then add bounded utilization and redundancy headroom. No useful GPU count or monthly price can be asserted without that workload and hardware benchmark. The current local-only model adapter does not become a remote GPU fleet by configuration. Secure distributed inference, workload identity, provider qualification and data-processing agreements need a separately reviewed adapter. Preserve model-digest checks and separate review/approval boundaries while scaling.

sections.title: Viral bursts, cost and recovery
sections.body: Serve immutable public assets through a CDN; reserve private API paths from public caching. Apply quotas, request bounds, tenant fairness and queue admission before expensive work. Autoscaling must have an approved maximum, dependency limits and rollback/backpressure behavior. Database saturation, GPU queues, logging/egress costs and third-party quotas are practical blockers. Budget alerts are not spending caps. One million 1MB initial downloads is approximately 1TB of transfer before repeat requests. Large-scale operation requires funded capacity, current regional pricing and workload-based estimates. Existing-host operation and future paid expansion are separate stages. See performance qualification, cost boundaries and reliability. References: PostgreSQL connection resources, FastAPI deployment concepts.

label: Reliability
title: Define the objective. Measure the experience.
description: Measure the public website, authenticated API and asynchronous work separately. Website probes must check expected content over public HTTPS. API probes check readiness and a controlled authenticated read. Track valid-request succ

sections.title: Service indicators
sections.body: Measure the public website, authenticated API and asynchronous work separately. Website probes must check expected content over public HTTPS. API probes check readiness and a controlled authenticated read. Track valid-request success, p50/p95/p99 latency, database pool saturation, queue depth/oldest age, worker heartbeat, lease recovery and delivery reconciliation. Define availability as good eligible events / all eligible events for request-based measurement, or good probe intervals / all scheduled intervals for time-based measurement. Do not interchange these denominators. Include eligible timeouts, 5xx and legitimate in-envelope 429s as failures. Exclude intentionally invalid/unauthorized requests consistently. Count planned maintenance against the initial objective; document any later contract-specific treatment. Report monitoring gaps as unknown coverage, never assumed uptime.

sections.title: Error budget and response
sections.body: Review the rolling window at least weekly. Alert on sustained outage and fast/slow error-budget burn using independent probes where available. When the budget is exhausted, prioritize reliability fixes, reduce risky releases and require recovery evidence before resuming changes. Record detection, impact, mitigation, restoration and corrective actions for incidents. Publish customer-relevant status without sensitive infrastructure details.

sections.title: Dependency and recovery limits
sections.body: The initial shared-host architecture has single-host/database dependency risk. Process restart and backups reduce recovery time but do not provide multi-zone failover. Local AI job latency has a separate queue/completion objective and must not make an otherwise healthy API appear ready for unlimited submissions. Initial proposed recovery objectives are RPO ≤24h and RTO ≤8h. Production timings and actual retained backup intervals must be recorded before claiming achieved recovery. A future multi-zone 99.9% objective allows 43m12s in 30 days and requires tested failover, dependency redundancy and funded operations. Reference: Google SRE: implementing SLOs, error-budget policy.

label: Operations
title: A release another person can operate.
description: Confirm the target host and available capacity using native inventories. Capture the current live files/configuration, compare with the prior local manifest, and reconcile drift before editing. Build from pinned dependencies with

sections.title: Prepare and deploy
sections.body: Confirm the target host and available capacity using native inventories. Capture the current live files/configuration, compare with the prior local manifest, and reconcile drift before editing. Build from pinned dependencies with the intended public origin. Run tests, types, lint, dependency/security scans and a fresh-context source review. Render deployment settings centrally; secrets remain in private environment files with restricted permissions. Create a new versioned release and manifest. Provision only the project-specific service account, database identities/storage, local inference and protected runner within approved existing capacity. Migrate using the dedicated migration role; web/worker environments receive only runtime credentials. Validate reverse-proxy/systemd/container settings before activation. Keep database/inference listeners private and public routes on the single HTTPS origin.

sections.title: Activate and validate
sections.body: Start database/inference, apply migrations, then start the API and worker. Check API schema readiness and actual model/sandbox qualification separately. Validate secure cookies, CSRF/Origin denial, outsider access denial, job completion, protected tests, distinct approvals and Git receipts through HTTPS. Switch the static release and proxy configuration only after preparation succeeds. Compare every deployed source/static/config byte with its local manifest. Preserve unrelated host services.

sections.title: Observe and respond
sections.body: Monitor HTTPS, eligible errors/latency, pool saturation, queue age, worker liveness, disk/memory, model latency and lease/reconciliation failures. Limit log size, redact credentials/content and define retention. Inspect error-budget burn before risky changes. Record incidents and remediation; public status must not disclose private topology or credentials.

sections.title: Rollback
sections.body: Keep the previous release, proxy/service configuration and encrypted database backup. Stop new admissions and let bounded work finish or cancel/reconcile it. Restore the previous frontend/API configuration and restart only project services. Database migrations are additive but schema compatibility must be checked; never blindly downgrade a database with accepted writes. If restoration is required, document lost-write scope against RPO, restore to an isolated database, verify rows/authorization, then reopen. Record actual RTO and final parity. Account creation is operator-managed: python -m app.manage create-user --email USER_EMAIL --name USER_NAME prompts privately for a password. Use --password-stdin only with a protected pipe; never put passwords in arguments/history. Repository grants are operator CLI actions. See self-hosting and disaster recovery.
